title: AlloyDB: CA Certs & Public DNS Info, Breaking Changes
summary: AlloyDB now provides crucial CA certificate information for secure PostgreSQL connections and public DNS names for instances. A new `publicDnsEnabled` option allows configuring public DNS. Be aware of breaking changes as `rootCaCert`, `certificateAuthorityInfo`, `networkInfo`, and `publicDnsName` are now read-only.
details:
AlloyDB introduces new output-only fields to enhance connectivity and security. The `Cluster` resource now includes `certificateAuthorityInfo`, which exposes a new `CertificateAuthorityInfo` schema containing the `rootCaCert`. This PEM-encoded root CA certificate is crucial for establishing secure PostgreSQL client connections using `sslmode=verify-full` or `sslmode=verify-ca`. Similarly, the `Instance` resource now provides `networkInfo`, which includes a new `InstanceNetworkInfo` schema with the `publicDnsName` for public connectivity. Additionally, you can now configure public DNS for instances via the new `publicDnsEnabled` boolean field within `InstanceNetworkConfig`.

**Breaking Change Alert:** Several properties have been transitioned to read-only status. Specifically, attempts to set `rootCaCert` within `CertificateAuthorityInfo`, the entire `certificateAuthorityInfo` object within `Cluster`, the `networkInfo` object within `Instance`, and `publicDnsName` within `InstanceNetworkInfo` will now result in errors. These fields are now strictly output-only, providing information but not allowing configuration. Developers must update their API calls to remove any attempts to modify these properties.
